I'm a long time Melee player, new time sm4sh player. I feel I have a pretty good grasp on the neutral in Melee, but when I move over to smash 4 I start to struggle. I find it hard with the lack of movement options to keep good spacing. In Melee you could wavedash back and gain space between you and your foe, you could dashdance to minimize commitment to approaches, but in smash 4 all you can really do (that I know of) is shorthop aerial, which can get pretty laggy.

Anyone have any tips for the neutral game?
[Smash 4] Can anyone help me with the neutral game?

You can always roll. They are not always safe, but they can be a good option to keep space and even change your facing. If you haven't looked into perfect pivoting then that is a good place to start. You can open lots of options that you don't have anything else comparable. To be fair, perfect pivoting is not amazing for distance. If distance is your issue, try looking at how you can walk and run. You can walk and immediately tilt for a more controlled speed dash attack substitute. Finally dash dancing is still around in Smash 4. You can use it for some of the same things you would want to use it for in mêlée, but it's not as great on most fighters. If everyone has the same tools (like walking, running, rolling, and no wave dashing) you just have to use your copies better.

Pivoting is super important in Sm4sh for spacing and power shielding is probably the most important tech you can learn. Check out Fatality's neutral game. He has one of the best neutral games I've seen from a non-sheik.

Pivoting allows you to get similar spacing options to wave dashing and most people are using it that way. I'm not sure about all characters but as you'll see in the video above, Captain Falcon has something similar to a dash dance.

If your opponent is shielding your short hop aerials, tomahawking (empty short hop to grab) is still very useful in this game.

New High School Teacher

After retiring, a former Gunny Sergeant in the Marine Corps took a new job a s a high school teacher.

Just before the school year started, he injured his back. He was required to wear a light plaster cast around the upper part of his body. Fortunately, the cast fit under his shirt and wasn't noticeable when he wore his suit coat.

On the first day of class, he found himself assigned to the toughest students in the school.

The smart-Aleck punks, having already heard the new teacher was a former Marine, were leery of him and he knew they would be testing his discipline in the classroom.

Walking confidently into the rowdy classroom, the new teacher opened the window wide and sat down at his desk. When a strong breeze made his tie flap, he picked up a stapler and stapled the tie to his chest. Dead silence ... The rest of the year went smoothly.
